'''Jeff Th. M. DeHosson''' is a materials scientist. He is a professor of [[Applied Physics]] at the Zernike Institute of Advanced Materials, [[University of Groningen]], the Netherlands.

DeHosson's research focuses on the physics of materials, electron microscopy, and nanostructured materials. He was awarded the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion|Knight of the Order of the Netherlands Lion]] and received the Eminent Scientist Medal from the [[Wessex Institute of Technology]]. He is also a fellow of the American Society for Metals and The Minerals, Metals & Materials Society, as well as an elected member of [[Academia Europaea]] and the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

==Education==
DeHosson completed his [[Candidate (degree)|candidate degree]] in [[Mathematics]] and Physical Sciences from the [[University of Utrecht]] in 1971. Later, in 1973, he earned his [[master's degree]] in [[Theoretical Physics]] and [[Chemical Physics]] from the same university. He completed his [[Ph.D.]] in [[Physics]] from the [[University of Groningen]] in 1976,<ref name=bio>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rug.nl/staff/j.t.m.de.hosson/cv?lang=en |title=prof. dr. J.T.M. (Jeff) de Hosson|website=University of Groningen|access-date=January 3, 2026}}</ref> with thesis supervisor André Wegener Sleeswijk.<ref name=act>{{Citeweb|url=https://actamaterialia.org/personnel/prof.-jeff-t.-m.-dehosson?utm_source |title=Prof. Jeff T. M. DeHosson|website=Acta Materialia|access-date=March 5, 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
DeHosson was appointed professor of [[Applied Physics]] at the [[University of Groningen]] by Royal Decree in 1977, a position he continues to hold. Between 1985 and 2015, he assumed the role of central departmental chair in Applied Physics, and also worked as chairman of the Executive Board of the Materials Science Centre of the University of Groningen. Additionally, he was a guest professor at [[Tsinghua University]] and the [[University of Science and Technology of China|University of Science and Technology]] in China, as well as at [[Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University]] in South Africa.<ref name=bio/>

DeHosson was an executive board member and founding member of the Netherlands Institute for Metals Research from 1997 to 2007. He was also an editor for the '' [[Acta Materialia]] Journals, Acta & [[Scripta Materialia]]'' from 1984 to 2026, as well as the Book Series from 2022 to 2028.<ref name=bio/>

==Research==
DeHosson's research focuses on advanced [[materials science]], with emphasis on understanding how internal imperfections and defects influence the behavior and performance of materials. He investigated how materials responded to [[Stress (mechanics)|stress]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Noori |first1=Hadi |last2=Jain |first2=Mukesh |last3=Nielsen |first3=Kent |last4=Brandys |first4=Frank |title=Delamination in deformed polymer laminated sheet metals |journal=International Journal of Adhesion and Adhesives |date=2018 |volume=85 |page=219 |doi=10.1016/j.ijadhadh.2018.06.014 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0143749618301696 |issn=0143-7496|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Deformation (engineering)|deformation]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sun |first1=B. A. |last2=Wang |first2=W. H. |title=The fracture of bulk metallic glasses |journal=Progress in Materials Science |date=1 October 2015 |volume=74 |page=236 |doi=10.1016/j.pmatsci.2015.05.002 |bibcode=2015PrMS...74..211S |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0079642515000584 |issn=0079-6425|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and external forces<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kumar |first1=Amitesh |last2=Roy |first2=Subhransu |title=Effect of three-dimensional melt pool convection on process characteristics during laser cladding |journal=Computational Materials Science |date=1 August 2009 |volume=46 |issue=2 |page=496 |doi=10.1016/j.commatsci.2009.04.002 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0927025609001608 |issn=0927-0256|url-access=subscription }}</ref> by examining their structural features at different length scales that affected their behavior.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Aifantis |first1=E.C. |title=Internal Length Gradient (ILG) Material Mechanics Across Scales and Disciplines |series=Advances in Applied Mechanics |date=1 January 2016 |volume=49 |page=25 |doi= 10.1016/bs.aams.2016.08.001 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/chapter/bookseries/abs/pii/S0065215616300023 |publisher=Elsevier|isbn=978-0-12-804779-8 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

An aspect of DeHosson's research is the dynamics of defects,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Qiao |first1=Junwei |last2=Jia |first2=Haoling |last3=Liaw |first3=Peter K. |title=Metallic glass matrix composites |journal=Materials Science and Engineering: R: Reports |date=1 February 2016 |volume=100 |page=60 |doi=10.1016/j.mser.2015.12.001 |bibcode=2016MSEnR.100....1Q |osti=1352097 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0927796X1500114X?fr=RR-2&ref=pdf_download&rr=9cb99f90dd3592f0 |issn=0927-796X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> including the [[dislocation]] storage in ultrafine and nanograined materials, which governs their mechanical behavior.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lu |first1=Xiaochong |last2=Zhang |first2=Xu |last3=Shi |first3=Mingxing |last4=Roters |first4=Franz |last5=Kang |first5=Guozheng |last6=Raabe |first6=Dierk |title=Dislocation mechanism based size-dependent crystal plasticity modeling and simulation of gradient nano-grained copper |journal=International Journal of Plasticity |date=2019 |volume=113 |page=14 |doi=10.1016/j.ijplas.2018.09.007 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S074964191830264X |issn=0749-6419|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He also showed that at micro- and nano-scales, plastic deformation was governed by unstable, discrete defect-driven events, leading to intermittent strain bursts rather than smooth, continuous flow.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ming |first1=Kaisheng |last2=Zhu |first2=Zhengwang |last3=Zhu |first3=Wenqing |last4=Fang |first4=Ben |last5=Wei |first5=Bingqiang |last6=Liaw |first6=Peter K. |last7=Wei |first7=Xiaoding |last8=Wang |first8=Jian |last9=Zheng |first9=Shijian |title=Enhancing strength and ductility via crystalline-amorphous nanoarchitectures in TiZr-based alloys |journal=Science Advances |date=11 March 2022 |volume=8 |issue=10 |page=4 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.abm2884 |pmid=35263125 |issn=2375-2548|pmc=8906574 |bibcode=2022SciA....8M2884M }}</ref>

DeHosson also contributed to the study of nanostructured materials,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Asoro |first1=M. A. |last2=Kovar |first2=D. |last3=Ferreira |first3=P. J. |title=Effect of surface carbon coating on sintering of silver nanoparticles: in situ TEM observations |journal=Chemical Communications |date=10 April 2014 |volume=50 |issue=37 |pages=4835–4838 |doi=10.1039/C4CC01547A |pmid=24687036 |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2014/cc/c4cc01547a |language=en |issn=1364-548X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> demonstrating that materials with high specific surface area were suitable for applications such as sensors and electrochemical actuators.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bencherifa |first1=Ismail |last2=Belkhettab |first2=Ilyas |last3=Chetoui |first3=Abdelmounaim |last4=Derkaoui |first4=Khaled |last5=Dabou |first5=Oussama |last6=Latreche |first6=Slimane |last7=Hamdoud |first7=Billel |title=Corrosion Characterization of Ti-6Al-4V Alloy After Constrained Groove Pressing and TiO2 Coating |journal=Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance |date=17 September 2025 |volume=35 |issue=7 |pages=7076–7096 |doi=10.1007/s11665-025-12091-8 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11665-025-12091-8|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In his book ''Metals as Clean Fuels'', he extended his research to energy-related applications, including hydrogen storage and the concept of nanostructured metals as scalable, CO₂-free fuels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/1522005415|title=Metals as clean fuels|website=WorldCat|access-date=February 10, 2026}}</ref> Moreover, he highlighted how processing parameters influenced both structure, such as nano-phases, and properties, including hardness and residual stress,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=Yuanjie |last2=Zhang |first2=Jinliang |last3=Yan |first3=Qian |last4=Zhang |first4=Lei |last5=Wang |first5=Min |last6=Song |first6=Bo |last7=Shi |first7=Yusheng |title=Amorphous alloy strengthened stainless steel manufactured by selective laser melting: Enhanced
